notes: All four players have actual habitat/wildlife viewports rather than one selected board plus tiny ledger icons.
Axial coordinates, grouped starter cells, six habitat edges and token-cell ids are explicit; no guessed fixed mosaic grid is drawn.
Landmarks/Rolling Hills/Rolling Rivers excluded. Solo and family/intermediate physical states are represented; no scenario-rule engine is supplied.
Current app fields are optional mapping hints; asset package includes independently meaningful physical-state JSON.
No hidden draw/bag identities or card-specific scores are inferred.

structureEvidence.location: official AEG product page; base-game overview
structureEvidence.verifiedFacts: 육각 서식지 타일과 야생동물 토큰을 조합해 각 플레이어 생태계를 확장하고, 종별 득점 목표에 따라 점수화하는 기본판 구조.

structureEvidence.location: official 2025 optimized base-game rulebook pp.3–5 components/setup; p.7 tile/token placement and Keystone reward; end-game turn count from official AEG rulebook search excerpt
structureEvidence.verifiedFacts: 85 habitat tiles including 25 Keystone tiles; 5 three-hex Starter Habitat tiles; 100 wildlife tokens (20 each of bear, elk, salmon, hawk, fox); 21 wildlife scoring cards; 25 Nature tokens; cloth bag and scorepad. Each player takes exactly 20 turns. Multiplayer tile draw setup is 20 per player plus 3: 43/63/83 tiles for 2/3/4 players. Setup reveals four habitat tiles and pairs them in order with four bag-drawn wildlife tokens; selects one scoring card per wildlife species; gives one starter tile per player. Nature tokens are shared supply and player holdings are recorded separately.

structureEvidence.access: pinned PDF; pp.3–7,9–11 directly rendered and viewed
structureEvidence.location: inventory/setup/placement pp.3–7; solo/variants p.10; scoring diagrams pp.9,11
structureEvidence.verifiedFacts: Five three-cell starters, one animal per hex, one/two habitats with orientation, four paired draft columns, solo discard/slide/refill separate from bag, family single scoring-card alternative.

assetScope: Full1–4player base table, every independent hex mosaic, exact draft columns, score cards, supplies, nature, solo removed pairs and resumable physical state; assets only.

players.selectedHabitatTileFormula: 20 per player plus 3 for the shared replacement supply in the official multiplayer setup
players.soloSetup: Use43habitat tiles as in2player setup, but only one starter and habitat stacks on the left. Before refill, remove the remaining rightmost tile/token pair from the game, slide remaining two pairs right, refill two left vacancies. Preserve remove/slide/refill checkpoints; discarded animals do not return to the bag.

coordinateSystem.vertices: angles -90+60*i degrees for i=0..5, clockwise in screen coordinates
coordinateSystem.edgeIndex: edge i joins vertex i to vertex (i+1)%6; edge outward angles -60,0,60,120,180,240 degrees
coordinateSystem.rotation60: k clockwise steps; local edge i moves to world edge (i+k)%6
coordinateSystem.starterObject: one physical object with three cells; rotate/translate all cells together, never edit their internal adjacency
coordinateSystem.ecosystemExtent: unbounded connected mosaic per player, no fictional finite board; overview fits/pans actual occupied cells
coordinateSystem.market: pair by columnIndex0..3; habitat slot bounding hexes and wildlife circles are separate physical targets

physicalInventory.selection: one card for each wildlife kind; unused cards return to box

habitatTile.identity: one hex tile; may show one or two habitat types and may be a Keystone with a wildlife icon

wildlifeToken.identity: one physical animal token from one of five equal species sets

ecosystemHex.adjacency: hex-edge adjacency; location/rotation is recorded without automatic legality checks

natureToken.rewardNote: Keystone placement/reward and market-choice effects are recorded as checkpoints; no automatic reward or legality execution.

scorepad.calculation: manual record only; no scoring engine in this asset

setup.wildlifeBag: All wildlife tokens are placed in the opaque cloth bag and randomized. Record known count/location only; never expose order/content unless the user supplies it.
setup.habitatPiles: Select and shuffle the player-count-dependent number of tiles; retain excluded/unused tiles as out-of-play state.
setup.scoringCards: Select one active card for each of the five wildlife kinds.
setup.starter: Deal one three-hex starter tile to each player; starter positions are not forced to a shared center.

turnCheckpoint: four habitat tiles face up and four wildlife tokens paired by column
selected pair or recorded Nature-token market action
habitat tile placed adjacent to the player mosaic with orientation and per-hex habitat split preserved
wildlife token placed on one exact unoccupied habitat hex, if placement is complete
Keystone reward / Nature-token holdings and market refill checkpoint
active player and turn count retained; exactly 20 turns per player in the standard game

preserve: all player mosaics and tile rotations
animal-token identity and exact hex location
four market pairings and pending selection
neverInfer: tile or animal identity from an unlabelled blank slot
a completed placement from a pending selection

tableModel.ruleAutomation: Not implemented. This model describes physical state and checkpoints, not placement legality, market actions, rewards, overpopulation handling, or score calculation.
tableModel.placementIdentity: Animal token references a physical cell, not just the starter object or a nearby tile. Starter three cells stay in one group. A split habitat stores its six edge habitats so orientation and actual habitat connections survive; no automatic colour-matching placement restriction is imposed.
tableModel.overpopulationCheckpoint: Temporarily wiped wildlife is kept outside the bag while replacements are drawn, then returned. Preserve this temporary set to avoid drawing returned tokens too early on resume.
tableModel.familyVariant: Record the chosen family/intermediate single scoring-card id and actual card position instead of selecting five species-specific scoring cards. Physical mosaic and draft structures stay the same; scoring is manual.

six ordered habitat edges and60degree rotation

diagramOnly: six player hexes are geometry examples, not initial setups or final size
colour/animal dots are neutral roles, not the contents of a particular printed tile

auxiliaryAssets.purpose: Original geometry examples only: one joined three-cell starter, a split habitat tile and an independently placed wildlife token; six edge-index points match JSON orientation. Not a printed starter identity.
